requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner, touching
requirements.evidence: The spike is at the cell's south-east junction (z≈+83 mm). The drawer fills the north half of the cell, away from that corner. The only spike site offered was that junction, and I could not confirm the two touch. check_build shows no mesh clash.

finish.summary: I built a drawer and a spike in cell 0,0, but they are not at the same corner. The cell is a south-half base with a drawer in its north half. Two full bases at 1,0 and 0,1 give the spike its three-cell junction. The spike sits at the south-east corner, and the drawer is on the opposite side of the cell. The mesh check reads clear. The two loose neighbour bases are unlocked, and I did not run lockJoints or capOpenFaces.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
